items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-07-23, 08-03
items.q: I lived right around the corner from Tony. I lived three doors.

ctx.x: Would Tony broadcast remote from the Parisian room or did you go to the station?

Tony had a five-day-a-week radio broadcast from the station that he played. He was a disc jockey. And then he had, gosh, it must have been about three broadcasts. Let's see, he had one on WWL and then he had, uh, one on WJMR, which was a station that he broadcast from, uh, disc jockey. And then he had a third one for the Armed Forces Network or something like that. So he did, spent the best part of his Sunday afternoons doing radio broadcasts, all from the Parisian room.

Yeah, well I can remember JMR and I would go in there to see him. He did his own commercials and played records. That's right. And I'd lend him some of my records from time to time. Uh-huh. I was working for Mercury Records, you know. Or William B. Allen, who was the distributor. Uh-huh. I could sort of check those dates out sometime, but I imagine there was plenty of documentation. Do you have any brothers and sisters?
